title: How long can an off-line zero survive the de Bruijn-Newman heat flow? An explicit unconditional lower bound for Lambda
summary: Let $\Lambda$ be the de Bruijn-Newman constant. The Riemann hypothesis (RH) is equivalent to $\Lambda\le 0$, and Rodgers and Tao proved $\Lambda\ge 0$. We ask how small $\Lambda$ can be if $\zeta$ has a zero $1/2+\delta+i\gamma$ with $\delta>0$. We use de Bruijn's strip, the zero dynamics of the Polymath project, and an explicit local zero count for the heat-flow deformations $H_\tau$ that we prove here.
